PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175.requirement: **Every repository ships one-command agent setup.** Each repository tracks an idempotent, non-interactive `scripts/bootstrap.sh` that installs a current uv, the pinned Python (`.python-version`, else the fleet standard), the locked environment (`uv sync --locked`, or the repository's equivalent), and the pre-commit and pre-push hooks, then prints the gate command `uvx pre-commit run --all-files`. The script never pipes a network response into a shell: uv comes from `pip install --user` (retrying with `--break-system-packages`) or the script stops with the install link, so the `supply-chain` rule SC-INSTALL-001 stays clean.
PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175.verification: `pipelines-hook agent-contract` reports `scripts/bootstrap.sh is not tracked` for a repository without it, reports SC-INSTALL-001 for a script containing `curl ... \| sh`, and passes under `--strict` for a conformant fixture.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R176.requirement: **Every repository carries the standard tool-neutral AGENTS.md section.** `AGENTS.md` holds the marked block `<!-- agent-contract:start -->` to `<!-- agent-contract:end -->` with the labels Owner boundary, Setup, Gates and Commits, and a link to the organization `AGENTS.md` at `https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md`. The block is tool-neutral; a tool-specific entry file such as `CLAUDE.md` only imports `AGENTS.md`. The connector scaffold in `universal-skills` generates both the script and the block.
PIPE-CONNSPEC-R176.verification: `pipelines-hook agent-contract --strict` fails for an `AGENTS.md` without the block, a missing label or a missing org link, and passes for a conformant fixture.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R177.requirement: **The agent-contract check is warn-level first.** The hook `agent-contract` (pre-push) reports findings and exits 0; `--strict` makes them blocking once the fleet has converged. It reads the tracked set only.
PIPE-CONNSPEC-R177.verification: The default run exits 0 with a `WARN` line for a nonconforming fixture, and `--strict` exits 1.

# Without this, `pre-commit install` wires ONLY the pre-commit hook, so `git push`
# runs nothing and every hook staged pre-push is silently dead code.
default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, pre-push]
default_language_version:
  python: python3
# Phase 0 dev-velocity contract (arbora-completion-program): a hook with no
# explicit `stages:` below is commit-only, never both.
default_stages: [pre-commit]
exclude: 'dotnet|node_modules'
ci:
  autofix_prs: true
  autoupdate_commit_msg: '[pre-commit.ci] pre-commit suggestions'
  autoupdate_schedule: 'monthly'

repos:
- repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
  rev: 3e8a8703264a2f4a69428a0aa4dcb512790b2c8c # v6.0.0
  hooks:
  - id: check-added-large-files
    args: ["--maxkb=2000"]
  - id: check-ast
    exclude: ^(tests/|test/|scripts/|script/)
  - id: check-yaml
    args: ["--unsafe"]
  - id: check-toml
  - id: check-json
  - id: fix-byte-order-marker
    exclude: .gitignore
  - id: check-merge-conflict
  - id: detect-private-key
  - id: trailing-whitespace
  - id: end-of-file-fixer
  - id: no-commit-to-branch
- repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
  rev: 38bfb07c0c64c304f47eb52090f8288150c77730  # frozen: v0.17.1
  hooks:
  - id: ruff-check
    args: ["--fix", "--ignore=E402,B008,E501"]
    exclude: ^(tests/|test/|scripts/|script/)
  - id: ruff-format
    exclude: ^(tests/|test/|scripts/|script/)
- repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
  rev: 2834ec6639549dd6796205c8f011dedcd587288b  # frozen: v2.4.0
  hooks:
  - id: mypy
    additional_dependencies: [pydantic==2.13.4, types-PyYAML==6.0.12.20260518, types-requests==2.33.0.20260518,
        types-setuptools==83.0.0.20260706]
    args: ["--ignore-missing-imports"]
- repo: https://github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture
  rev: 258fe6a1974e89a2add9a45519a9e9dd9f46154e  # frozen: v2.16
  hooks:
  - id: vulture
    pass_filenames: false
    args: [".", "--min-confidence", "95", "--exclude", "node_modules,dotnet,.venv,venv,node_modules,.git,build,dist"]
    require_serial: true
- repo: https://github.com/codespell-project/codespell
  rev: 57b21406f092110c18776e39b0bda50d37c945c8  # frozen: v2.4.3
  hooks:
  - id: codespell
    args: ["-L", "ans,linar,nam,tread,ot,", "--ignore-words=.codespellignore"]
    exclude: ^(tests/|test/|scripts/|script/|.*lock.*)
- repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/bandit
  rev: 92ae8b82fb422a639f0ed8d99e96cea769594e08 # 1.9.4
  hooks:
  - id: bandit
    args: ["--skip", "B101,B404,B603"]
    exclude: ^(tests/|test/|scripts/|script/|__tests__/)
- repo: https://github.com/nbQA-dev/nbQA
  rev: f96ec7f3b26a32619435686eb5813235f7e3327e  # frozen: 1.9.1
  hooks:
  - id: nbqa-ruff
    args: ["--fix"]
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: uv-lock
    name: uv-lock (verify, never mutate)
    entry: uv lock --check
    language: system
    files: ^(uv\.lock|pyproject\.toml|uv\.toml)$
    pass_filenames: false
    stages: [pre-push, manual]
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: mermaid-validate
    name: mermaid-validate
    entry: mermaid-validate
    language: node
    additional_dependencies: ['@zabaca/mermaid-validate@1.0.1']
    types: [markdown]
    pass_filenames: true
  - id: check-agent-standards
    name: check agent standards
    entry: |-
      bash -c 'for f in $(find . -type f -name "agent_server.py" -not -path "*/\.venv/*" -not -path "*/__pycache__/*"); do grep -q "warnings.filterwarnings" "$f" && grep -q "file=sys.stderr" "$f" || { echo "Missing warnings.filterwarnings or file=sys.stderr in $f"; exit 1; }; done'
    language: system
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true
  - id: env-var-drift
    name: check env-var/config drift
    entry: bash -c 'if [ -f uv.lock ]; then uv run python -m agent_connector_sdk.mcp.env_drift --check; else python -m agent_connector_sdk.mcp.env_drift --check; fi'
    language: system
    pass_filenames: false
    files: ^(README\.md|\.env\.example|mcp_config.*\.json|.*/mcp_config.*\.json|docker/.*compose.*\.ya?ml|.*/auth\.py|.*/mcp_server\.py)$
  - id: check-cli-help
    name: check cli help
    entry: |-
      bash -c 'for f in $(find . -type f \( -name "mcp_server.py" -o -name "agent_server.py" \) -not -path "*/\.venv/*" -not -path "*/__pycache__/*"); do mod=$(echo "$f" | sed -e "s/^\.\///" -e "s/\.py$//" -e "s/\//./g"); uv run --frozen --all-extras python -m "$mod" --help >/dev/null || exit 1; done'
    language: system
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true
  - id: check-bumpversion
    name: validate bumpversion config
    entry: |-
      bash -c 'if [ -f ".bumpversion.cfg" ]; then bump2version patch --dry-run --allow-dirty; fi'
    language: system
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: pytest
    name: pytest
    entry: bash -c 'test_target="tests"; for d in tests/unit test/unit tests test; do if [ -d "$d" ]; then test_target="$d"; break; fi; done; if [ -f uv.lock ]; then uv run --all-extras pytest "$test_target" -q --tb=short -m "not slow" --timeout=60; else pytest "$test_target" -q --tb=short -m "not slow" --timeout=60; fi'
    language: system
    types: [python]
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true
    stages: [pre-push, manual]
- repo: https://github.com/AleksaC/hadolint-py
  rev: 6e7504451511eaeb62a3e7f14d63b0296cbf86eb  # frozen: v2.15.1
  hooks:
  - id: hadolint
    args:
    - --ignore=DL3008
    - --ignore=DL3015
    - --ignore=DL3009
    - --ignore=DL4006
    - --ignore=SC2102
- repo: https://github.com/IamTheFij/docker-pre-commit
  rev: f626253b23de45412865c07fd076ff95d4cd77a7 # v3.0.1
  hooks:
  - id: docker-compose-check

- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: verify-api-integration
    name: Verify API-to-MCP Integration Coverage
    entry: python scripts/verify_api_integration.py --local
    language: system
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: security-sanitizer
    name: Security and Garbage Sanitizer
    entry: python scripts/security_sanitizer.py
    language: python
    pass_filenames: false
    always_run: true

implementation.content:
"""agent-contract: the repository gives a cold agent one-command setup and the standard AGENTS.md section.

Warn level (exit 0): a missing ``scripts/bootstrap.sh`` (or one that trips the
SC-INSTALL-001/002 installer rules, such as ``curl ... | sh``), a missing
``AGENTS.md``, or an ``AGENTS.md`` without the marked standard section is
reported but does not fail. ``--strict`` makes the findings blocking, for the
day the fleet has converged. Reads the tracked set only, never the filesystem.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from pipelines_hooks.core.gitenv import repo_root
from pipelines_hooks.core.tracked import tracked_paths
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.dependencies import installer_findings
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.finding import Source

START = "<!-- agent-contract:start -->"
END = "<!-- agent-contract:end -->"
ORG_AGENTS = "https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md"
#: Labels the standard section carries, in the order the standard states them.
LABELS = ("**Owner boundary:**", "**Setup:**", "**Gates:**", "**Commits:**")


def inspect(root: Path, paths: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every finding for one repository (an empty list means conformant)."""
    findings: list[str] = []
    if "scripts/bootstrap.sh" not in paths:
        findings.append("scripts/bootstrap.sh is not tracked")
    else:
        script = (root / "scripts/bootstrap.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        findings.extend(
            f"scripts/bootstrap.sh:{f.line}: {f.rule} {f.message}"
            for f in installer_findings(Source(root.name, "scripts/bootstrap.sh", script))
        )
    if "AGENTS.md" not in paths:
        findings.append("AGENTS.md is not tracked")
        return findings
    text = (root / "AGENTS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    start, end = text.find(START), text.find(END)
    if start < 0 or end < start:
        findings.append(f"AGENTS.md lacks the {START} ... {END} section")
        return findings
    block = text[start:end]
    findings.extend(f"agent-contract section lacks {label}" for label in LABELS if label not in block)
    if ORG_AGENTS not in block:
        findings.append(f"agent-contract section does not link {ORG_AGENTS}")
    return findings


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-contract", description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
    parser.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="fail on findings instead of warning")
    arguments = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = repo_root(arguments.root)
    findings = inspect(root, tracked_paths(root))
    if not findings:
        print("agent-contract: conformant (scripts/bootstrap.sh and the standard AGENTS.md section)")
        return 0
    level = "FAIL" if arguments.strict else "WARN"
    print(f"{level}: agent-contract (reference/ci-standard.md, Agent contract):")
    for finding in findings:
        print(f"  {finding}")
    return 1 if arguments.strict else 0

plan.content:
# Architecture — PIPE-CONNSPEC

## Approach

Each connector copies the reference callers named in PIPE-CONNSPEC-R004 and the hook configuration used in this repository. Nothing new is built here. Adoption is tracked per connector through the four child requirements, and the generated status rolls each connector up from its children.

## Order

Land the specs tree and hooks first, then the Pages caller, then the skill section, so each connector's dashboard shows real states from its first publish.

## Landing attribution compatibility

The generator uses Git trailer parsing in the existing single history scan, with historical Spec subjects, ranges and shorthand retained. Existing merged_head and landed_in receipts remain supported: they do not preserve enough provenance to distinguish valid migrations from old parser mistakes. Correct known false receipts through targeted review rather than global invalidation.

## Amendment: retired identities (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R006 reconciles ownership moves with permanent requirement IDs. Reuse the status generator retirement parser in the standard gate. Preserve the old row as RETIRED and name its replacement; active rows still obey prefix checks. This does not repair or retire existing rows automatically.

## Repository ownership

Resolve the repository slug offline from origin, or a sole configured remote when origin is absent. This authoritative identity overrides stale generated ownership. If remote identity cannot be established, keep the prior owner, with checkout basename only as a final fallback. Keep legacy landing validation independent of identity correction.

## Amendment: CI prose comparison (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R007 closes the clean-index gap in hosted `ste-staged` runs. Reuse sanitized Git access, commit resolution, and bounded event JSON loading. Resolve explicit refs first, then GitHub event bases, then pre-commit refs outside GitHub Actions. New-ref pushes and manual runs check the last commit with full history. Never guess when a requested base is absent. Preserve local staged-index checks and per-file `(code, message)` debt subtraction.

## Generated identity

The generator reuses `standard.check_title` for canonical spec identity. A valid title governs the generated ID. Historical specs without a canonical title retain their fallback; requirement identities and landing receipts are unchanged.

### 2026-10-16: withdraw invalid verification evidence

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R001 permits a narrow evidence-only correction without losing its Spec IDs.
A Spec-Withdraw trailer names the IDs, and Spec-Withdrawal-Reason records why acceptance evidence is invalid.
The whole PR range must preserve requirements and executable source.
Only actual Rust comment bindings may be removed, with owning plan additions, task reopening and generated status updates.
Every withdrawn ID must lose an existing binding and retain its reason in the owning plan.
Unknown IDs, missing reasons, altered code, requirements, modes, workflow or build configuration fail closed.
Other IDs still require ordinary acceptance bindings. Status remains generated from the corrected evidence.

## Amendment: exact standard-ID renumbering (2026-10-23)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R011 extends the existing alias loader, not trailer acceptance rules. Parse current requirement rows with the shared parser before accepting an exact standard-ID alias. The source must have no current requirement row, including a retired tombstone; the target must be an active row, not a prose mention or another alias. Reject source or target collisions with retired prefixes. Existing prefix aliases and pre-standard exact aliases retain their one-hop behavior. The ordinary trailer gate still requires a bound target test and refuses unrelated unknown IDs. A renumbering fixture checks the historical range and the current PR range independently, and preserves the original landing receipt under the new ID.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R012 to R016 add competency-question priority. A competency question is an ordinary `EG-CQ-` row, so the Depends-on graph already carries the signal. The scorer in `priority.py` is shared by the status generator and the architecture page.

## Amendment: distinguish CQ paths from architecture links (2026-10-25)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R016 labels the existing unserved filter “No CQ dependency path”.
Its explanation states the direction: CQ → Depends-on → requirement. The label
does not report missing architecture placement or implementation links. Keep
the existing filter, scores, classification, requirement states and evidence.
This wording change adds no dependencies and changes no competency questions.

## Amendment: canonical aggregate-hook mapping (2026-10-26)

The child `.2` verification rows use the phrase "the three spec hooks" for the
canonical spec gate contract. The current connector template publishes the
single `spec` aggregate hook alongside the other aggregate gates. At the
provider source, `pipelines_hooks/cli.py:73` defines that aggregate as
`spec-standard`, `spec-decomposition`, `spec-status`, and `spec-trailers`.
Therefore `spec` is the accepted canonical replacement for the three literal
spec hooks in the connector adoption rows; the validation test must assert this
source mapping before binding a `.2` row. This mapping changes no consumer
configuration or runtime behavior.

    repo.commit({"scripts/bootstrap.sh": clean})

reference.content:
# CI standard (shared pieces)

Pipelines owns the reusable parts of the fleet CI standard; each repository calls them at `@main`. The checks they run are the [gate standard](gate-standard.md).

- `gates_pipeline.yml`: one `gates` job. Pull requests run the caller's pre-commit file at the commit stage and the pre-push stage over `--from-ref/--to-ref`; a main push sets `all-files: true`. Then the affected-test subset from `pr-test-scope`. Inputs: `config`, `ci-config`, `test-scope`, `src-root`, `runner`, `rust`, `all-files`, `extra-manual-hooks`, `skip-hooks`, `setup-command`, `docs-only-paths`, `timeout-minutes`. Every input has a default. On `push` events the workflow adds `spec-trailers` to `SKIP`: trailers are a property of pull request commits and a squash merge does not carry them; pull request runs always enforce the hook.
- `gates_pipeline.yml` skips the pre-push `tests-fast` hook (and the deprecated `fast-tests` id) when `test-scope` is set, because its affected-test step runs the same subset without the local cap.
- `connector_pr_pipeline.yml` (PIPE-RELEASE-R011): the connector pull request workflow. It wraps `gates_pipeline.yml` with `config: .pre-commit-config.yaml`, `stages: pre-commit` and a 10-minute cap, then runs the affected unit tests. It never publishes. Input `sync-args` (default `--all-extras --all-groups`) sets the `uv sync --frozen` arguments for a connector whose extras cannot all build on a CPU runner. A connector adds a caller on `pull_request`.
- `container_pipeline.yml` ends with a verification step (PIPE-RELEASE-R012). A connector release publishes the PyPI version and the `<version>-mcp` image, and the run fails when either is missing. The `release-standard` hook (PIPE-RELEASE-R013) warns when a connector lacks `docker/Dockerfile` or an enabled `container_pipeline.yml` job.
- Release speed (PIPE-RELEASE-R014 to R016). `container_pipeline.yml` reuses one named BuildKit builder (`ci-shared`) per runner pod instead of creating and removing one per job, replaces it when it will not boot, and prunes its local cache to 30 GB; the per-target registry `buildcache-*` tags stay. Wheel readiness proves the runtime profiles concurrently (at most four, declared order kept) and installs with `--no-compile`; the public-index, wheel-only and no-cache rules are unchanged. `publish-python-package` keeps uv downloads and managed interpreters in the runner tool cache.
- `main_pipeline.yml`: the main and release-tag workflow. Job `tests` runs the full suite; job `supply-chain` runs one dependency audit (`pip-audit` over the runtime lock, or `cargo deny check advisories` with `rust: true`). Inputs: `test-scope`, `runner`, `rust`, `setup-command`, `timeout-minutes`. It never publishes; release workflows stay with each repository.
- `advisory_pipeline.yml`: the weekly advisory workflow. It runs the advisory `pipelines-hook` gates, codespell, vulture, bandit and any `extra-commands`, writes one Markdown report to the job summary and the `advisory-report` artifact, and never fails. Inputs: `gates`, `python-tools`, `extra-commands`, `scanners`, `runner`.
- Concurrency belongs to the caller: PR group `pr-<workflow>-<number>` and main group `main-<workflow>` cancel superseded runs; release and pages groups never cancel. The workflow header carries the copyable block.
- Input `docs-only-paths` (default empty): space-separated bash patterns of docs and spec paths. When every file in a pull request diff matches one, the job passes right after checkout. A caller that sets it drops `paths-ignore` from `pull_request` and has no skip companion, so exactly one `gates / gates` check exists. A skip run under the same name can then never mask a failing real run on a mixed code and docs pull request.
- `templates/workflows/gates-skip.yml`: the older companion that reports the required `gates` check for docs/spec-only changes that `paths-ignore` skips. On a mixed pull request both workflows report the same name; prefer `docs-only-paths`.
- `python_pipeline.yml` input `require-tag` (default `false`): when `true` the job fails before building unless the ref is a `v*` tag. A release workflow triggered by `push: tags: ['v*']` sets it.
- Hook `fast-tests` (pre-push): affected tests only, 120 s cap, base from `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF`.
- Local hooks follow the [pre-commit standard](precommit-standard.md): only fast checks at pre-commit and pre-push. The CI-only gates are in `.config/ci-gates.yaml`, and the `ci-config` input of `gates_pipeline.yml` runs them.

## Required status check

A repository that adopts `gates_pipeline.yml` through a caller job named `gates` requires the single status check `gates / gates` in its branch ruleset. The docs and spec-only skip companion reports the same name.

## Agent contract

Every repository gives a cold agent the same setup and the same orientation (PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175 to R177):

- `scripts/bootstrap.sh` is idempotent and non-interactive. It installs a current uv (via `pip install --user`, never a piped network installer: SC-INSTALL-001), the Python pinned in `.python-version` (default 3.14), runs `uv sync --locked` (plain `uv sync` until the repository has a `uv.lock`), installs the pre-commit and pre-push hooks, and prints the gate command. A repository with extra setup (sibling pins, native builds) extends the script and keeps these steps.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the block between `<!-- agent-contract:start -->` and `<!-- agent-contract:end -->`. The block states the **Owner boundary** (with a link to [ecosystem boundaries](ecosystem-boundaries.md)), **Setup** (`scripts/bootstrap.sh`), **Gates** (`uvx pre-commit run --all-files`), **Commits** (Spec trailer, assisting-agent `Co-Authored-By:` trailer, explicit staging, own Git identity) and a link to the [organization AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md). The text is tool-neutral. Content outside the markers belongs to the repository. `CLAUDE.md`, where present, only imports `@AGENTS.md`.
- The pre-push hook `agent-contract` flags a missing `scripts/bootstrap.sh` or one that trips SC-INSTALL-001/002, a missing `AGENTS.md`, or a missing or incomplete block. It warns (exit 0) until the fleet has converged; `--strict` blocks.

implementation.content:
"""agent-contract: the repository gives a cold agent one-command setup and the standard AGENTS.md section.

Warn level (exit 0): a missing ``scripts/bootstrap.sh`` (or one that trips the
SC-INSTALL-001/002 installer rules, such as ``curl ... | sh``), a missing
``AGENTS.md``, or an ``AGENTS.md`` without the marked standard section is
reported but does not fail. ``--strict`` makes the findings blocking, for the
day the fleet has converged. Reads the tracked set only, never the filesystem.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from pipelines_hooks.core.gitenv import repo_root
from pipelines_hooks.core.tracked import tracked_paths
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.dependencies import installer_findings
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.finding import Source

START = "<!-- agent-contract:start -->"
END = "<!-- agent-contract:end -->"
ORG_AGENTS = "https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md"
#: Labels the standard section carries, in the order the standard states them.
LABELS = ("**Owner boundary:**", "**Setup:**", "**Gates:**", "**Commits:**")


def inspect(root: Path, paths: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every finding for one repository (an empty list means conformant)."""
    findings: list[str] = []
    if "scripts/bootstrap.sh" not in paths:
        findings.append("scripts/bootstrap.sh is not tracked")
    else:
        script = (root / "scripts/bootstrap.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        findings.extend(
            f"scripts/bootstrap.sh:{f.line}: {f.rule} {f.message}"
            for f in installer_findings(Source(root.name, "scripts/bootstrap.sh", script))
        )
    if "AGENTS.md" not in paths:
        findings.append("AGENTS.md is not tracked")
        return findings
    text = (root / "AGENTS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    start, end = text.find(START), text.find(END)
    if start < 0 or end < start:
        findings.append(f"AGENTS.md lacks the {START} ... {END} section")
        return findings
    block = text[start:end]
    findings.extend(f"agent-contract section lacks {label}" for label in LABELS if label not in block)
    if ORG_AGENTS not in block:
        findings.append(f"agent-contract section does not link {ORG_AGENTS}")
    return findings


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-contract", description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
    parser.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="fail on findings instead of warning")
    arguments = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = repo_root(arguments.root)
    findings = inspect(root, tracked_paths(root))
    if not findings:
        print("agent-contract: conformant (scripts/bootstrap.sh and the standard AGENTS.md section)")
        return 0
    level = "FAIL" if arguments.strict else "WARN"
    print(f"{level}: agent-contract (reference/ci-standard.md, Agent contract):")
    for finding in findings:
        print(f"  {finding}")
    return 1 if arguments.strict else 0

# Architecture — PIPE-CONNSPEC

## Approach

Each connector copies the reference callers named in PIPE-CONNSPEC-R004 and the hook configuration used in this repository. Nothing new is built here. Adoption is tracked per connector through the four child requirements, and the generated status rolls each connector up from its children.

## Order

Land the specs tree and hooks first, then the Pages caller, then the skill section, so each connector's dashboard shows real states from its first publish.

## Landing attribution compatibility

The generator uses Git trailer parsing in the existing single history scan, with historical Spec subjects, ranges and shorthand retained. Existing merged_head and landed_in receipts remain supported: they do not preserve enough provenance to distinguish valid migrations from old parser mistakes. Correct known false receipts through targeted review rather than global invalidation.

## Amendment: retired identities (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R006 reconciles ownership moves with permanent requirement IDs. Reuse the status generator retirement parser in the standard gate. Preserve the old row as RETIRED and name its replacement; active rows still obey prefix checks. This does not repair or retire existing rows automatically.

## Repository ownership

Resolve the repository slug offline from origin, or a sole configured remote when origin is absent. This authoritative identity overrides stale generated ownership. If remote identity cannot be established, keep the prior owner, with checkout basename only as a final fallback. Keep legacy landing validation independent of identity correction.

## Amendment: CI prose comparison (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R007 closes the clean-index gap in hosted `ste-staged` runs. Reuse sanitized Git access, commit resolution, and bounded event JSON loading. Resolve explicit refs first, then GitHub event bases, then pre-commit refs outside GitHub Actions. New-ref pushes and manual runs check the last commit with full history. Never guess when a requested base is absent. Preserve local staged-index checks and per-file `(code, message)` debt subtraction.

## Generated identity

The generator reuses `standard.check_title` for canonical spec identity. A valid title governs the generated ID. Historical specs without a canonical title retain their fallback; requirement identities and landing receipts are unchanged.

### 2026-10-16: withdraw invalid verification evidence

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R001 permits a narrow evidence-only correction without losing its Spec IDs.
A Spec-Withdraw trailer names the IDs, and Spec-Withdrawal-Reason records why acceptance evidence is invalid.
The whole PR range must preserve requirements and executable source.
Only actual Rust comment bindings may be removed, with owning plan additions, task reopening and generated status updates.
Every withdrawn ID must lose an existing binding and retain its reason in the owning plan.
Unknown IDs, missing reasons, altered code, requirements, modes, workflow or build configuration fail closed.
Other IDs still require ordinary acceptance bindings. Status remains generated from the corrected evidence.

## Amendment: exact standard-ID renumbering (2026-10-23)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R011 extends the existing alias loader, not trailer acceptance rules. Parse current requirement rows with the shared parser before accepting an exact standard-ID alias. The source must have no current requirement row, including a retired tombstone; the target must be an active row, not a prose mention or another alias. Reject source or target collisions with retired prefixes. Existing prefix aliases and pre-standard exact aliases retain their one-hop behavior. The ordinary trailer gate still requires a bound target test and refuses unrelated unknown IDs. A renumbering fixture checks the historical range and the current PR range independently, and preserves the original landing receipt under the new ID.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R012 to R016 add competency-question priority. A competency question is an ordinary `EG-CQ-` row, so the Depends-on graph already carries the signal. The scorer in `priority.py` is shared by the status generator and the architecture page.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R016 labels the existing unserved filter “No CQ dependency path”.
Its explanation states the direction: CQ → Depends-on → requirement. The label
does not report missing architecture placement or implementation links. Keep
the existing filter, scores, classification, requirement states and evidence.
This wording change adds no dependencies and changes no competency questions.

## Amendment: canonical aggregate-hook mapping (2026-10-26)

The child `.2` verification rows use the phrase "the three spec hooks" for the
canonical spec gate contract. The current connector template publishes the
single `spec` aggregate hook alongside the other aggregate gates. At the
provider source, `pipelines_hooks/cli.py:73` defines that aggregate as
`spec-standard`, `spec-decomposition`, `spec-status`, and `spec-trailers`.
Therefore `spec` is the accepted canonical replacement for the three literal
spec hooks in the connector adoption rows; the validation test must assert this
source mapping before binding a `.2` row. This mapping changes no consumer
configuration or runtime behavior.

from tests.hooks import conftest

@pytest.mark.spec("PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175")

def test_bootstrap_that_pipes_a_network_response_into_a_shell_is_flagged(repo: Repo, capsys) -> None:

reference.content:
# CI standard (shared pieces)

Pipelines owns the reusable parts of the fleet CI standard; each repository calls them at `@main`. The checks they run are the [gate standard](gate-standard.md).

- `gates_pipeline.yml`: one `gates` job. Pull requests run the caller's pre-commit file at the commit stage and the pre-push stage over `--from-ref/--to-ref`; a main push sets `all-files: true`. Then the affected-test subset from `pr-test-scope`. Inputs: `config`, `ci-config`, `test-scope`, `src-root`, `runner`, `rust`, `all-files`, `extra-manual-hooks`, `skip-hooks`, `setup-command`, `docs-only-paths`, `timeout-minutes`. Every input has a default. On `push` events the workflow adds `spec-trailers` to `SKIP`: trailers are a property of pull request commits and a squash merge does not carry them; pull request runs always enforce the hook.
- `gates_pipeline.yml` skips the pre-push `tests-fast` hook (and the deprecated `fast-tests` id) when `test-scope` is set, because its affected-test step runs the same subset without the local cap.
- `connector_pr_pipeline.yml` (PIPE-RELEASE-R011): the connector pull request workflow. It wraps `gates_pipeline.yml` with `config: .pre-commit-config.yaml`, `stages: pre-commit` and a 10-minute cap, then runs the affected unit tests. It never publishes. Input `sync-args` (default `--all-extras --all-groups`) sets the `uv sync --frozen` arguments for a connector whose extras cannot all build on a CPU runner. A connector adds a caller on `pull_request`.
- `container_pipeline.yml` ends with a verification step (PIPE-RELEASE-R012). A connector release publishes the PyPI version and the `<version>-mcp` image, and the run fails when either is missing. The `release-standard` hook (PIPE-RELEASE-R013) warns when a connector lacks `docker/Dockerfile` or an enabled `container_pipeline.yml` job.
- Release speed (PIPE-RELEASE-R014 to R016). `container_pipeline.yml` reuses one named BuildKit builder (`ci-shared`) per runner pod instead of creating and removing one per job, replaces it when it will not boot, and prunes its local cache to 30 GB; the per-target registry `buildcache-*` tags stay. Wheel readiness proves the runtime profiles concurrently (at most four, declared order kept) and installs with `--no-compile`; the public-index, wheel-only and no-cache rules are unchanged. `publish-python-package` keeps uv downloads and managed interpreters in the runner tool cache.
- `main_pipeline.yml`: the main and release-tag workflow. Job `tests` runs the full suite; job `supply-chain` runs one dependency audit (`pip-audit` over the runtime lock, or `cargo deny check advisories` with `rust: true`). Inputs: `test-scope`, `runner`, `rust`, `setup-command`, `timeout-minutes`. It never publishes; release workflows stay with each repository.
- `advisory_pipeline.yml`: the weekly advisory workflow. It runs the advisory `pipelines-hook` gates, codespell, vulture, bandit and any `extra-commands`, writes one Markdown report to the job summary and the `advisory-report` artifact, and never fails. Inputs: `gates`, `python-tools`, `extra-commands`, `scanners`, `runner`.
- Concurrency belongs to the caller: PR group `pr-<workflow>-<number>` and main group `main-<workflow>` cancel superseded runs; release and pages groups never cancel. The workflow header carries the copyable block.
- Input `docs-only-paths` (default empty): space-separated bash patterns of docs and spec paths. When every file in a pull request diff matches one, the job passes right after checkout. A caller that sets it drops `paths-ignore` from `pull_request` and has no skip companion, so exactly one `gates / gates` check exists. A skip run under the same name can then never mask a failing real run on a mixed code and docs pull request.
- `templates/workflows/gates-skip.yml`: the older companion that reports the required `gates` check for docs/spec-only changes that `paths-ignore` skips. On a mixed pull request both workflows report the same name; prefer `docs-only-paths`.
- `python_pipeline.yml` input `require-tag` (default `false`): when `true` the job fails before building unless the ref is a `v*` tag. A release workflow triggered by `push: tags: ['v*']` sets it.
- Hook `fast-tests` (pre-push): affected tests only, 120 s cap, base from `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF`.
- Local hooks follow the [pre-commit standard](precommit-standard.md): only fast checks at pre-commit and pre-push. The CI-only gates are in `.config/ci-gates.yaml`, and the `ci-config` input of `gates_pipeline.yml` runs them.

## Required status check

A repository that adopts `gates_pipeline.yml` through a caller job named `gates` requires the single status check `gates / gates` in its branch ruleset. The docs and spec-only skip companion reports the same name.

## Agent contract

Every repository gives a cold agent the same setup and the same orientation (PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175 to R177):

- `scripts/bootstrap.sh` is idempotent and non-interactive. It installs a current uv (via `pip install --user`, never a piped network installer: SC-INSTALL-001), the Python pinned in `.python-version` (default 3.14), runs `uv sync --locked` (plain `uv sync` until the repository has a `uv.lock`), installs the pre-commit and pre-push hooks, and prints the gate command. A repository with extra setup (sibling pins, native builds) extends the script and keeps these steps.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the block between `<!-- agent-contract:start -->` and `<!-- agent-contract:end -->`. The block states the **Owner boundary** (with a link to [ecosystem boundaries](ecosystem-boundaries.md)), **Setup** (`scripts/bootstrap.sh`), **Gates** (`uvx pre-commit run --all-files`), **Commits** (Spec trailer, assisting-agent `Co-Authored-By:` trailer, explicit staging, own Git identity) and a link to the [organization AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md). The text is tool-neutral. Content outside the markers belongs to the repository. `CLAUDE.md`, where present, only imports `@AGENTS.md`.
- The pre-push hook `agent-contract` flags a missing `scripts/bootstrap.sh` or one that trips SC-INSTALL-001/002, a missing `AGENTS.md`, or a missing or incomplete block. It warns (exit 0) until the fleet has converged; `--strict` blocks.

Delivery status is generated, never hand-edited, and each requirement is in exactly one of the states SPECIFIED, LANDED, VERIFIED, or RETIRED. New landings use explicit Spec trailers or historical Spec subjects, never unrelated prose or none exemption reasons; historical receipts retain their existing validation. implementation.content:
"""agent-contract: the repository gives a cold agent one-command setup and the standard AGENTS.md section.

Warn level (exit 0): a missing ``scripts/bootstrap.sh`` (or one that trips the
SC-INSTALL-001/002 installer rules, such as ``curl ... | sh``), a missing
``AGENTS.md``, or an ``AGENTS.md`` without the marked standard section is
reported but does not fail. ``--strict`` makes the findings blocking, for the
day the fleet has converged. Reads the tracked set only, never the filesystem.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from pipelines_hooks.core.gitenv import repo_root
from pipelines_hooks.core.tracked import tracked_paths
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.dependencies import installer_findings
from pipelines_hooks.supply_chain.finding import Source

START = "<!-- agent-contract:start -->"
END = "<!-- agent-contract:end -->"
ORG_AGENTS = "https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md"
#: Labels the standard section carries, in the order the standard states them.
LABELS = ("**Owner boundary:**", "**Setup:**", "**Gates:**", "**Commits:**")


def inspect(root: Path, paths: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Every finding for one repository (an empty list means conformant)."""
    findings: list[str] = []
    if "scripts/bootstrap.sh" not in paths:
        findings.append("scripts/bootstrap.sh is not tracked")
    else:
        script = (root / "scripts/bootstrap.sh").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        findings.extend(
            f"scripts/bootstrap.sh:{f.line}: {f.rule} {f.message}"
            for f in installer_findings(Source(root.name, "scripts/bootstrap.sh", script))
        )
    if "AGENTS.md" not in paths:
        findings.append("AGENTS.md is not tracked")
        return findings
    text = (root / "AGENTS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    start, end = text.find(START), text.find(END)
    if start < 0 or end < start:
        findings.append(f"AGENTS.md lacks the {START} ... {END} section")
        return findings
    block = text[start:end]
    findings.extend(f"agent-contract section lacks {label}" for label in LABELS if label not in block)
    if ORG_AGENTS not in block:
        findings.append(f"agent-contract section does not link {ORG_AGENTS}")
    return findings


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-contract", description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path.cwd())
    parser.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="fail on findings instead of warning")
    arguments = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = repo_root(arguments.root)
    findings = inspect(root, tracked_paths(root))
    if not findings:
        print("agent-contract: conformant (scripts/bootstrap.sh and the standard AGENTS.md section)")
        return 0
    level = "FAIL" if arguments.strict else "WARN"
    print(f"{level}: agent-contract (reference/ci-standard.md, Agent contract):")
    for finding in findings:
        print(f"  {finding}")
    return 1 if arguments.strict else 0

# Architecture — PIPE-CONNSPEC

## Approach

Each connector copies the reference callers named in PIPE-CONNSPEC-R004 and the hook configuration used in this repository. Nothing new is built here. Adoption is tracked per connector through the four child requirements, and the generated status rolls each connector up from its children.

## Order

Land the specs tree and hooks first, then the Pages caller, then the skill section, so each connector's dashboard shows real states from its first publish.

## Landing attribution compatibility

The generator uses Git trailer parsing in the existing single history scan, with historical Spec subjects, ranges and shorthand retained. Existing merged_head and landed_in receipts remain supported: they do not preserve enough provenance to distinguish valid migrations from old parser mistakes. Correct known false receipts through targeted review rather than global invalidation.

## Amendment: retired identities (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R006 reconciles ownership moves with permanent requirement IDs. Reuse the status generator retirement parser in the standard gate. Preserve the old row as RETIRED and name its replacement; active rows still obey prefix checks. This does not repair or retire existing rows automatically.

## Repository ownership

Resolve the repository slug offline from origin, or a sole configured remote when origin is absent. This authoritative identity overrides stale generated ownership. If remote identity cannot be established, keep the prior owner, with checkout basename only as a final fallback. Keep legacy landing validation independent of identity correction.

## Amendment: CI prose comparison (2026-10-11)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R007 closes the clean-index gap in hosted `ste-staged` runs. Reuse sanitized Git access, commit resolution, and bounded event JSON loading. Resolve explicit refs first, then GitHub event bases, then pre-commit refs outside GitHub Actions. New-ref pushes and manual runs check the last commit with full history. Never guess when a requested base is absent. Preserve local staged-index checks and per-file `(code, message)` debt subtraction.

## Generated identity

The generator reuses `standard.check_title` for canonical spec identity. A valid title governs the generated ID. Historical specs without a canonical title retain their fallback; requirement identities and landing receipts are unchanged.

### 2026-10-16: withdraw invalid verification evidence

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R001 permits a narrow evidence-only correction without losing its Spec IDs.
A Spec-Withdraw trailer names the IDs, and Spec-Withdrawal-Reason records why acceptance evidence is invalid.
The whole PR range must preserve requirements and executable source.
Only actual Rust comment bindings may be removed, with owning plan additions, task reopening and generated status updates.
Every withdrawn ID must lose an existing binding and retain its reason in the owning plan.
Unknown IDs, missing reasons, altered code, requirements, modes, workflow or build configuration fail closed.
Other IDs still require ordinary acceptance bindings. Status remains generated from the corrected evidence.

## Amendment: exact standard-ID renumbering (2026-10-23)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R011 extends the existing alias loader, not trailer acceptance rules. Parse current requirement rows with the shared parser before accepting an exact standard-ID alias. The source must have no current requirement row, including a retired tombstone; the target must be an active row, not a prose mention or another alias. Reject source or target collisions with retired prefixes. Existing prefix aliases and pre-standard exact aliases retain their one-hop behavior. The ordinary trailer gate still requires a bound target test and refuses unrelated unknown IDs. A renumbering fixture checks the historical range and the current PR range independently, and preserves the original landing receipt under the new ID.

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R012 to R016 add competency-question priority. A competency question is an ordinary `EG-CQ-` row, so the Depends-on graph already carries the signal. The scorer in `priority.py` is shared by the status generator and the architecture page.

## Amendment: distinguish CQ paths from architecture links (2026-10-25)

PIPE-CONNSPEC-R016 labels the existing unserved filter “No CQ dependency path”.
Its explanation states the direction: CQ → Depends-on → requirement. The label
does not report missing architecture placement or implementation links. Keep
the existing filter, scores, classification, requirement states and evidence.
This wording change adds no dependencies and changes no competency questions.

## Amendment: canonical aggregate-hook mapping (2026-10-26)

The child `.2` verification rows use the phrase "the three spec hooks" for the
canonical spec gate contract. The current connector template publishes the
single `spec` aggregate hook alongside the other aggregate gates. At the
provider source, `pipelines_hooks/cli.py:73` defines that aggregate as
`spec-standard`, `spec-decomposition`, `spec-status`, and `spec-trailers`.
Therefore `spec` is the accepted canonical replacement for the three literal
spec hooks in the connector adoption rows; the validation test must assert this
source mapping before binding a `.2` row. This mapping changes no consumer
configuration or runtime behavior.

# CI standard (shared pieces)

Pipelines owns the reusable parts of the fleet CI standard; each repository calls them at `@main`. The checks they run are the [gate standard](gate-standard.md).

- `gates_pipeline.yml`: one `gates` job. Pull requests run the caller's pre-commit file at the commit stage and the pre-push stage over `--from-ref/--to-ref`; a main push sets `all-files: true`. Then the affected-test subset from `pr-test-scope`. Inputs: `config`, `ci-config`, `test-scope`, `src-root`, `runner`, `rust`, `all-files`, `extra-manual-hooks`, `skip-hooks`, `setup-command`, `docs-only-paths`, `timeout-minutes`. Every input has a default. On `push` events the workflow adds `spec-trailers` to `SKIP`: trailers are a property of pull request commits and a squash merge does not carry them; pull request runs always enforce the hook.
- `gates_pipeline.yml` skips the pre-push `tests-fast` hook (and the deprecated `fast-tests` id) when `test-scope` is set, because its affected-test step runs the same subset without the local cap.
- `connector_pr_pipeline.yml` (PIPE-RELEASE-R011): the connector pull request workflow. It wraps `gates_pipeline.yml` with `config: .pre-commit-config.yaml`, `stages: pre-commit` and a 10-minute cap, then runs the affected unit tests. It never publishes. Input `sync-args` (default `--all-extras --all-groups`) sets the `uv sync --frozen` arguments for a connector whose extras cannot all build on a CPU runner. A connector adds a caller on `pull_request`.
- `container_pipeline.yml` ends with a verification step (PIPE-RELEASE-R012). A connector release publishes the PyPI version and the `<version>-mcp` image, and the run fails when either is missing. The `release-standard` hook (PIPE-RELEASE-R013) warns when a connector lacks `docker/Dockerfile` or an enabled `container_pipeline.yml` job.
- Release speed (PIPE-RELEASE-R014 to R016). `container_pipeline.yml` reuses one named BuildKit builder (`ci-shared`) per runner pod instead of creating and removing one per job, replaces it when it will not boot, and prunes its local cache to 30 GB; the per-target registry `buildcache-*` tags stay. Wheel readiness proves the runtime profiles concurrently (at most four, declared order kept) and installs with `--no-compile`; the public-index, wheel-only and no-cache rules are unchanged. `publish-python-package` keeps uv downloads and managed interpreters in the runner tool cache.
- `main_pipeline.yml`: the main and release-tag workflow. Job `tests` runs the full suite; job `supply-chain` runs one dependency audit (`pip-audit` over the runtime lock, or `cargo deny check advisories` with `rust: true`). Inputs: `test-scope`, `runner`, `rust`, `setup-command`, `timeout-minutes`. It never publishes; release workflows stay with each repository.
- `advisory_pipeline.yml`: the weekly advisory workflow. It runs the advisory `pipelines-hook` gates, codespell, vulture, bandit and any `extra-commands`, writes one Markdown report to the job summary and the `advisory-report` artifact, and never fails. Inputs: `gates`, `python-tools`, `extra-commands`, `scanners`, `runner`.
- Concurrency belongs to the caller: PR group `pr-<workflow>-<number>` and main group `main-<workflow>` cancel superseded runs; release and pages groups never cancel. The workflow header carries the copyable block.
- Input `docs-only-paths` (default empty): space-separated bash patterns of docs and spec paths. When every file in a pull request diff matches one, the job passes right after checkout. A caller that sets it drops `paths-ignore` from `pull_request` and has no skip companion, so exactly one `gates / gates` check exists. A skip run under the same name can then never mask a failing real run on a mixed code and docs pull request.
- `templates/workflows/gates-skip.yml`: the older companion that reports the required `gates` check for docs/spec-only changes that `paths-ignore` skips. On a mixed pull request both workflows report the same name; prefer `docs-only-paths`.
- `python_pipeline.yml` input `require-tag` (default `false`): when `true` the job fails before building unless the ref is a `v*` tag. A release workflow triggered by `push: tags: ['v*']` sets it.
- Hook `fast-tests` (pre-push): affected tests only, 120 s cap, base from `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF`.
- Local hooks follow the [pre-commit standard](precommit-standard.md): only fast checks at pre-commit and pre-push. The CI-only gates are in `.config/ci-gates.yaml`, and the `ci-config` input of `gates_pipeline.yml` runs them.

## Required status check

A repository that adopts `gates_pipeline.yml` through a caller job named `gates` requires the single status check `gates / gates` in its branch ruleset. The docs and spec-only skip companion reports the same name.

## Agent contract

Every repository gives a cold agent the same setup and the same orientation (PIPE-CONNSPEC-R175 to R177):

- `scripts/bootstrap.sh` is idempotent and non-interactive. It installs a current uv (via `pip install --user`, never a piped network installer: SC-INSTALL-001), the Python pinned in `.python-version` (default 3.14), runs `uv sync --locked` (plain `uv sync` until the repository has a `uv.lock`), installs the pre-commit and pre-push hooks, and prints the gate command. A repository with extra setup (sibling pins, native builds) extends the script and keeps these steps.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the block between `<!-- agent-contract:start -->` and `<!-- agent-contract:end -->`. The block states the **Owner boundary** (with a link to [ecosystem boundaries](ecosystem-boundaries.md)), **Setup** (`scripts/bootstrap.sh`), **Gates** (`uvx pre-commit run --all-files`), **Commits** (Spec trailer, assisting-agent `Co-Authored-By:` trailer, explicit staging, own Git identity) and a link to the [organization AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Knuckles-Team/.github/blob/main/AGENTS.md). The text is tool-neutral. Content outside the markers belongs to the repository. `CLAUDE.md`, where present, only imports `@AGENTS.md`.
- The pre-push hook `agent-contract` flags a missing `scripts/bootstrap.sh` or one that trips SC-INSTALL-001/002, a missing `AGENTS.md`, or a missing or incomplete block. It warns (exit 0) until the fleet has converged; `--strict` blocks.
